"Penulisan
GAME TITLE: ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED
1. KONSEP GAME
Buat sebuah game 2D RPG Action Adventure dengan gaya pixel art yang sangat detail, menggabungkan elemen:
Dark Fantasy
Open World
Dungeon Exploration
Monster Hunting
RPG Leveling
Random Ability System
Character Progression
Boss Battle
Loot and Equipment
Story-driven Adventure
Game memiliki inspirasi mekanisme perkembangan karakter seperti Solo Leveling, tetapi harus mempunyai identitas, cerita, desain dunia, dan sistem orisinal.
Pemain memulai sebagai manusia biasa yang tiba-tiba mendapatkan sebuah sistem misterius.
Tidak semua orang memiliki kekuatan yang sama. Ketika pertama kali membangkitkan sistem, pemain mendapatkan satu kemampuan secara acak.
Kemampuan tersebut bisa Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, atau Divine.
Tidak ada pilihan untuk menentukan kekuatan awal. Sistem harus melakukan random generation.
2. GRAFIK DAN VISUAL
Gunakan:
2D Pixel Art berkualitas tinggi.
Resolusi pixel konsisten dan tajam.
Gaya pixel art seperti game RPG indie modern.
Animasi karakter yang halus.
Detail lingkungan sangat kaya.
Efek skill dengan partikel pixel.
Pencahayaan dinamis.
Bayangan monster dan karakter.
Efek hujan, kabut, malam, siang, dan perubahan cuaca.
Efek damage dan critical hit.
Visual harus terlihat seperti game pixel RPG premium, bukan pixel art sederhana atau kotak-kotak tanpa detail.
Kamera menggunakan top-down 2D atau 3/4 perspective.
Buat karakter, monster, NPC, dungeon, bangunan, pohon, senjata, dan lingkungan memiliki sprite masing-masing.
3. RANDOM AWAKENING SYSTEM
Ketika memulai permainan:
Pemain membuat nama karakter.
Pemain memilih penampilan dasar.
Pemain memasuki prolog cerita.
Sistem muncul untuk pertama kalinya.
Sistem melakukan Random Awakening.
Pemain mendapatkan satu kekuatan secara permanen.
Contoh kemampuan:
COMMON:
Enhanced Strength
Minor Regeneration
Night Vision
Wind Step
UNCOMMON:
Flame Manipulation
Ice Spear
Shadow Movement
Lightning Touch
RARE:
Blood Control
Spatial Slash
Phantom Clone
Soul Absorption
EPIC:
Gravity Manipulation
Necromancy
Time Perception
Dragon Transformation
LEGENDARY:
Void Manipulation
Monarch's Authority
Eternal Flame
Celestial Sword
MYTHIC:
Reality Distortion
World Devourer
Absolute Shadow
Divine Creation
DIVINE:
Origin Authority
Absolute System
Primordial Existence
Setiap kemampuan harus memiliki:
Nama.
Deskripsi.
Rarity.
Level kemampuan.
Damage.
Cooldown.
Mana cost.
Passive effect.
Active skill.
Evolution path.
Kekuatan tidak boleh hanya berbeda nama. Setiap kekuatan memiliki mekanisme gameplay berbeda.
4. STATUS CHARACTER
Buat panel status RPG:
Level
EXP
HP
MP
Strength
Agility
Vitality
Intelligence
Perception
Luck
Defense
Attack Power
Critical Chance
Critical Damage
Setiap naik level, pemain mendapatkan status points.
Pemain bisa mendistribusikan poin secara bebas.
Tambahkan sistem statistik tersembunyi seperti:
Potential
Soul Capacity
Adaptability
Resistance
5. SYSTEM INTERFACE
Sediakan UI sistem futuristik berwarna biru gelap dengan aksen ungu.
Menu utama:
[ STATUS ] [ SKILLS ] [ INVENTORY ] [ EQUIPMENT ] [ QUEST ] [ DUNGEON ] [ BESTIARY ] [ ACHIEVEMENTS ] [ MAP ] [ SETTINGS ]
Ketika sistem memberikan pesan, munculkan kotak notifikasi seperti:
[SYSTEM]
Congratulations, Player.
Your awakening has been completed.
Unique Ability Acquired: [ RANDOM ABILITY ]
Rarity: [RANDOM RARITY]
Your journey begins now.
6. COMBAT SYSTEM
Buat sistem pertarungan real-time.
Fitur:
Basic attack.
Heavy attack.
Dodge.
Dash.
Skill combination.
Critical attack.
Enemy targeting.
Boss mechanics.
Combo counter.
Stamina management.
Mana management.
Pemain bisa bertarung menggunakan:
Sword
Dual Sword
Dagger
Spear
Greatsword
Bow
Staff
Magic
Bare Hands
Setiap senjata memiliki animasi dan gaya bertarung berbeda.
7. DUNGEON SYSTEM
Dungeon muncul secara acak di berbagai wilayah.
Jenis dungeon:
Forest Dungeon
Ancient Ruins
Underground Cave
Forgotten Castle
Abyss Dungeon
Dragon Nest
Cursed Temple
Shadow Realm (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8:

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: set -euo pipefail

The workspace is empty of game code. Need to build a complete playable game. Let's see the environment: node, playwright-cli, etc.

We need to build a 2D pixel art RPG action adventure. This is a huge request, but we need a playable game with many systems. Best approach: single-page HTML game using Canvas 2D, vanilla JS, procedurally generated pixel art sprites (drawn at runtime to offscreen canvases), with game systems: character creation, random awakening, stats, skill tree, inventory, equipment, quests, dungeons, bestiary, achievements, map, settings, real-time combat, weapons, bosses, loot, day/night weather.

Could use Three.js? Requirement says top-down 2D pixel art. Canvas 2D is ideal.

Need quality visuals: detailed pixel art sprites. We can procedurally generate sprites with pixel drawing code. Need character, monsters, NPCs, dungeon, buildings, trees, weapons, environment. Rich detail, particles, lighting, shadows, rain/fog, day/night.

Need UI dark blue with purple accents; system menu with multiple tabs.

Need playable: WASD movement, mouse aim, attacks, dodge, skills, combos, stamina/mana, boss fight, dungeon. Start flow: title -> character creation (name, appearance) -> prologue -> random awakening -> gameplay.

Need verify via Playwright screenshots. Need perhaps build is static; can serve via python http.server or node. Let's inspect environment and package availability.

Let me plan architecture:

Files:
- index.html
- styles.css
- js/main.js, maybe modular files: engine.js, sprites.js, world.js, entities.js, abilities.js, ui.js, game.js
- Use ES modules, served over http.

Given complexity, split into modules to keep manageable:
1. `src/utils.js` - RNG, math, helpers.
2. `src/art.js` - procedural sprite generation (pixel art) for player, monsters, NPCs, trees, rocks, buildings, weapons, tiles, effects.
3. `src/abilities.js` - ability database across rarities with mechanics.
4. `src/data.js` - items, enemies, dungeons, quests, bestiary, achievements, NPC dialogue, appearance options.
5. `src/world.js` - world generation (open world chunks, biomes), dungeon generation, collision, lighting.
6. `src/entities.js` - Player, Enemy, NPC, Projectile, effects.
7. `src/ui.js` - HUD, system UI overlay, menus, notifications, character creation.
8. `src/game.js` - main loop, input, camera, combat, quests, save/load, spawning.
9. `index.html`, `styles.css`.

That's a lot. Need to implement carefully and test.

Given time/tokens, we should build robust but compact. Aim maybe 4000-6000 lines total. We have plenty of token budget but need to be efficient. Could implement in fewer files ~ maybe 3000 lines.

Let's think about gameplay loop:
- Title screen with logo, starfield, "New Game", "Continue" if save, "Controls".
- Character creation: name input, appearance grid (hair style, hair color, cloak color), difficulty? Start.
- Prologue dialogue overlay: narration about eclipse, system awakening. Then random ability card reveals with rarity animation. Show ability details. Start in village at night.
- Gameplay: top-down world, camera follows. NPC "Elder" gives quest to clear Forest Dungeon; village has blacksmith (equipment), merchant? Quest.
- World map: large-ish 3200x2400 with village, forest, ruins, cave entrance, castle, etc. Static but hand-designed via tile map generation. Random dungeon entrances appear (maybe static plus random). Simpler: overworld with zones. Dungeon entrances placed. Entering loads procedural dungeon level based on seed, with rooms/corridors, monsters, loot, boss room.
- Combat: mouse aim, LMB basic combo, RMB heavy or skill; Space dodge; Q/E/R skills based on ability; 1-5 potions? Ability active skills unique mechanics. Need at least generic active for every ability with distinct effect. Could implement 4 skills based on ability kit with different behaviors. Simplicity: each ability defines `skills` array with type parameter; combat engine interprets types: projectile, aoe, dash, beam, summon, buff, chain, teleport, etc. Each ability has unique passive stats and skill names/descriptions.
- Enemies: slimes, wolves, bandits, skeletons, wraiths, golems, dragon boss. AI: idle/chase/attack, telegraphs, health bars, loot.
- XP/leveling, stat points. Status panel with allocate buttons.
- Skills panel: ability details, evolution path, level up ability with skill points? Could use "Essence" from kills. Maybe ability level up via ability points on level.
- Inventory/equipment: weapons/armor/accessories with stats, equip, sell? Keep simple but functional (equip, use potions).
- Bestiary: kills count, discovered entries.
- Achievements: triggered.
- Map: minimap + fullscreen map with markers.
- Settings: volume slider, screen shake, weather toggle? save/reset.
- Save to localStorage.
- Weather/day-night cycle + rain particles + fog + dynamic lighting.
- Boss: Forest Guardian / Eclipse Warden in dungeon. Boss mechanics: phases, attacks, telegraphs. Dungeon completion rewards ability evolution material.

We need visual quality. Procedural pixel art:
- Tile size 32? For detailed pixel art, use internal resolution 480x270 scaled up? Top-down 3/4 at 16x16 tiles with high detail is tough. Could render world at 16px tiles scaled 3x to viewport, with sprites 16-32px. Pixel art crisp. But "detailed" — we can draw tiles with many pixel details.

Better: internal resolution viewport e.g. 640x360, render at integer scale to fit screen, top-down 3/4. Tiles 32px in internal res. Character sprites 24x32. Procedural drawings with shading. UI drawn in DOM at full res (crisp text) with pixel font? Use Google font? Network may be unreliable. Use CSS pixel font families fallback, maybe embed font? We can use system monospace with letter spacing. Could draw UI in DOM (blue/purple sci-fi) with custom CSS; good.

Canvas internal resolution 480x270 might look very pixelated at 1280 width (2.66x) with non-integer scaling. We can set canvas CSS width to viewport, internal resolution based on device width/3 capped. Use `image-rendering: pixelated`. To be crisp: internal res = Math.floor(width / scale) where scale = max(1, floor(min(width/960,height/540)))... Hmm. Simpler: internal resolution 640x360 and CSS scale (object-fit). At 1280 wide, ×2 exact. Screenshots likely 1280x720. Good. Canvas 640x360, CSS full window, image-rendering pixelated. For other sizes, use CSS scale to cover with letterbox.

World rendering: draw floor tiles, decorations, entities sorted by y. Lighting: create offscreen light canvas at half resolution? We can draw ambient darkness overlay via globalCompositeOperation 'multiply' using a low-res light map. During daytime, little darkness. Night: dark blue overlay with light holes around player, braziers, spells. Use canvas compositing.

Procedural sprite generation:
- Use a helper `makeCanvas(w,h)` and draw with rects. Pixel art sprites as arrays? Writing arrays for all sprites is heavy. Instead procedural pixel drawing with seeded noise + shapes, which can look good.
- Character: 4-direction? Top-down/3/4, use one side/front view and flip. Walk animation via bobbing legs/arms. Generate a sprite sheet at runtime for player with parts (hair, cloak color). Draw 24x32 sprites for 2-frame walk + idle + attack frames. Could draw each frame procedurally per tint. Simpler: draw player directly on canvas each frame with pixel shapes, using time for walk. But "sprites each" requirement. We can generate sprite sheets into offscreen canvases for each appearance + direction; monsters generated too. This is fine.

Let me design art module:

Utilities:
```js
function px(ctx,x,y,w,h,color){ctx.fillStyle=color;ctx.fillRect(x,y,w,h);}
function makeSprite(w,h,drawFn){ const c=document.createElement('canvas'); c.width=w;c.height=h; const x=c.getContext('2d'); x.imageSmoothingEnabled=false; drawFn(x,w,h); return c; }
```

Palette: colors with variations. Shading: base color, highlight, shadow.

Player sprite 20x28? At 32 tile size, character 22x30. Draw body: boots, legs, torso cloak, arms, head, hair, eyes, weapon. Four directions (down, up, left, right) × 4 frames? Could do idle(2), walk(4), attack(3). Generate with limb offsets. Maybe 12 frames per direction; 4 dirs × 10 = 40 canvases per appearance. Only generate chosen appearance once. Acceptable. Or draw dynamically but call it sprite? Better generate.

Simplify directions: down, up, side (flip for left). Frames: idle (2), walk (4), attack (3). = 9 per dir x3 = 27 sprites. Draw at 24x32. Weapon overlay maybe separate.

We can make character art more detailed: hair styles 4 (short, long, spiky, hood), colors; cloak colors. Use `drawHumanoid(ctx, opts, dir, frame)`.

Monsters: generate canvas per type and animation frame (2-4). Types:
- Gloom Slime (blob with eyes, moss)
- Dire Wolf (quadruped detailed)
- Bandit (humanoid with mask)
- Skeleton (bones)
- Wraith (floating cloak)
- Stone Golem
- Venom Spider
- Dragon boss (large 96x96)
- Eclipse Warden boss (humanoid big)

Could draw them procedurally with decent detail.

Environment:
- Tile types: grass, dirt, stone, water, sand, path, floor dungeon, wall, void.
- Create tile textures 32x32 generated with seeded noise and details: grass blades, flowers, pebbles; path with stones; water animated? Use two frames.
- Trees, bushes, rocks, houses, fences, lamps, ruins pillars, gravestones, cave entrances, castle etc as sprites.
- Village: houses drawn procedurally with roofs, windows, doors, chimney.
- Lighting: lamps at night.

World gen:
Maybe handcraft a map with functions: base grass, a village at center-left, forest region right, lake bottom-left, ruins top-right, caves. Use deterministic hash noise for tile variation. Add collision for water, trees, buildings, walls. Entities: NPCs, enemies spawned per zone, dungeon entrances. Dungeon entrances: Forest Dungeon, Ancient Ruins, Underground Cave, Forgotten Castle, Abyss, Dragon Nest, Cursed Temple (7 types) placed around. Requirement includes "Shadow Realm (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)" — weird note. We can include locked Shadow Realm portal mention as "requires 3D client" joke? Probably just include as a special endgame dungeon with a note. Maybe add a "Shadow Realm" portal that's locked until level 20 with label "3D client required" — but that's odd. Better include 7 dungeons, plus a sealed Shadow Realm rift with "DORMANT — 3D realm not yet stabilized" as a lore teaser. That satisfies mention without 3D.

Dungeon generation per type: procedural rooms + corridors grid. Render dungeon floors/walls using generated tiles. Enemies, chests, shrine, boss room. Exit portal back to overworld. Boss defined per dungeon with mechanics. Dungeon level scaling.

We need ability system with 30 abilities (3-4 per rarity × 7). Each with distinct mechanics. That's a lot but can define real skill behaviors for each using a small set of archetypes and distinct tuning/visuals. Requirement says each power must have different gameplay mechanics, not just names. We can make each family distinct: projectile, aoe, dash, beam, summon, buff, chain, teleport, drain, time slow, gravity pull, transform, clone, etc. Define 5 skills per ability? That's 150 definitions. Too much. Each ability: 3 active skills + passive + evolution. 28 abilities × 3 = 84 skills. Could generate programmatically from ability "kit" templates with unique names. But mechanisms need distinct within rarity. We can define a table with per-ability `style` and skills generated using style mechanics. Yet to be defensible, build 28 abilities with 2-3 skills each, each skill specifying behavior from ~15 behaviors and element/color/visual. Names/descriptions custom. That's manageable maybe 500 lines in data file.

Let's list abilities with rarity and mechanics:
Common:
1. Enhanced Strength — melee shockwave, berserk buff, ground slam. Passive +attack.
2. Minor Regeneration — heal over time, regen aura, cleanse. Passive HP regen.
3. Night Vision — reveal map radius, shadow bolt? Passive crit in dark, night speed. Mechanic: toggle true sight, mark enemies, fear.
4. Wind Step — dash with afterimages, gust projectile, evasion buff. Passive move speed/dodge.

Uncommon:
5. Flame Manipulation — fireball, flame wall, meteor.
6. Ice Spear — piercing lance, frost nova (slow), ice armor.
7. Shadow Movement — teleport behind target, shadow clone decoy, dark burst.
8. Lightning Touch — chain lightning, static field, blink strike.

Rare:
9. Blood Control — blood lance (drain), blood shield, domain (lifesteal).
10. Spatial Slash — teleport slash, void rift (pull), dimensional blade (pierce).
11. Phantom Clone — summon clones that fight, swap positions, mirror barrage.
12. Soul Absorption — drain beam, soul nova, consume corpse? Summon soul orb.

Epic:
13. Gravity Manipulation — gravity well pull, levitate slam, singularity.
14. Necromancy — raise skeleton minion, corpse explosion, death coil.
15. Time Perception — slow time bubble, haste self, temporal rewind (heal/dash back).
16. Dragon Transformation — dragon breath cone, wings dash, transform buff (temporary dragon form).

Legendary:
17. Void Manipulation — void orb, black hole, nullify shield.
18. Monarch's Authority — command wave (stun), shadow army summons, domination aura.
19. Eternal Flame — phoenix dash, flame pillars, rebirth passive.
20. Celestial Sword — sword rain, celestial beam, divine slash.

Mythic:
21. Reality Distortion — warp terrain/teleport swap with enemy, mirror realm (invuln), collapse.
22. World Devourer — devour projectile (heal), maw aoe, consume buff.
23. Absolute Shadow — shadow form (invuln movement), shadow spikes, umbra execution.
24. Divine Creation — create barrier, create turret construct, genesis heal zone.

Divine:
25. Origin Authority — rewrite: reset cooldowns, absolute control (freeze enemies), origin blast.
26. Absolute System — system override: execute low HP enemies, buff all stats, cooldown freeze.
27. Primordial Existence — primordial form (massive buffs), creation wave, erase.

That's 27. Good.

Each ability defines:
- id, name, rarity, desc, flavor, passive {text, apply stat mods}, evolution path text, color, and skills [{name, desc, behavior, mana, cooldown, damage, radius, speed, duration, level?}].
- Ability level scales damage; evolve at ability level 5/10? Use "Essence" to level ability. We can implement ability leveling with "SKILL" points earned per player level; level up skills increases damage/heal and cooldown reduction.

Skill behaviors implemented:
- projectile (single/pierce/explode)
- multiProjectile / barrage
- aoe (nova at player or target)
- dash (damage along path)
- beam (line damage)
- chain (chain lightning)
- teleport (blink to cursor / behind enemy)
- summon (clone/minion/turret)
- buff (stat mods, timed)
- shield
- heal
- drain (beam lifesteal)
- pull (gravity well)
- slow (time bubble)
- ground (delayed meteor / pillars)
- transform (dragon form)
- execute (low HP)
- reset (cooldowns)
- swap
- mark/reveal
- wall (flame wall)
- fear
- trap?

Implement generic effect engine supporting these. Each skill may have `kind`, `tags`. Distinctness via combinations.

Passive: apply player stat modifiers, plus some special (regen, lifesteal, dodge chance, crit at night, phoenix revive, etc.). Keep code in player stats.

Combat details:
- Player attack: LMB -> 3-hit melee combo based on weapon; or bow/staff projectiles. Weapon determines range/arc/damage/speed. Mouse aim.
- RMB heavy attack: charged? Just heavy swing with knockback, costs stamina.
- Space dodge/dash i-frames.
- Shift sprint? Stamina.
- 1-3 skills Q E R? Requirement skill combination. Use Q/E/R for ability skills, F for ultimate maybe ability's 3rd. Let's do Q, E, R (3 skills); LMB attack, RMB heavy, Space dodge, Shift sprint.
- 1/2 potions? Hotbar items maybe H health potion, M mana potion. Or UI buttons.
- Combo counter increases damage; resets after 3s.
- Crit.
- Stamina for heavy/dodge; mana for skills.

Enemy AI: types with ranged/melee/charger. Boss with phases and telegraphed attacks (rings, cones, projectiles, summons). Need functional boss.

Progression:
- XP -> level, +5 stat points, +1 skill point.
- Stats allocate affecting derived: attack, defense, HP, MP, crit, etc.
- Loot: items with rarity and stats, dropped from enemies/chests. Equip weapons/armor/amulet. Inventory limited? Keep 40 slots.
- Gold, buy potions from merchant via shop UI maybe. Could implement simple shop interaction.

NPC interactions: press E near NPC -> dialogue with quest / shop / heal. Quest log tracks.

Story: intro, village elder, first dungeon, then "Eclipse Warden" final boss at Cursed Temple? Open world. Quests: "The Awakening" -> talk to Elder; "Shadows in the Grove" -> clear Forest Dungeon; "Fragments of the Eclipse" -> collect 3 Eclipse Sigils from dungeon bosses; "The Last Awakened" -> defeat Eclipse Monarch in Cursed Temple (locked until 3 sigils). That's a complete game arc. Could include final boss and ending screen.

Achievements: First Blood, Level 5, Dungeon Delver, Collector, Boss Slayer, Awakened, Combo 20, etc.

Bestiary: discovered and kills, descriptions.

UI:
- HUD: top-left portrait + HP/MP/Stamina bars, level; top-right minimap, day/time, weather; bottom-left ability icons cooldown; bottom-center combo; bottom-right quest tracker; notifications & damage numbers in canvas maybe DOM.
- System overlay: full screen dark glass, left vertical tabs with 10 tabs, content panes. Keyboard shortcut Tab opens system; menu tabs I/J/K etc. Use DOM for menus.
- Notifications: system messages top center with blue/purple styling.
- Damage numbers floating in world (canvas text with pixel font).
- Loot pickup prompts.

messages.text:
"Penulisan
GAME TITLE: ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED
1. KONSEP GAME
Buat sebuah game 2D RPG Action Adventure dengan gaya pixel art yang sangat detail, menggabungkan elemen:
Dark Fantasy
Open World
Dungeon Exploration
Monster Hunting
RPG Leveling
Random Ability System
Character Progression
Boss Battle
Loot and Equipment
Story-driven Adventure
Game memiliki inspirasi mekanisme perkembangan karakter seperti Solo Leveling, tetapi harus mempunyai identitas, cerita, desain dunia, dan sistem orisinal.
Pemain memulai sebagai manusia biasa yang tiba-tiba mendapatkan sebuah sistem misterius.
Tidak semua orang memiliki kekuatan yang sama. Ketika pertama kali membangkitkan sistem, pemain mendapatkan satu kemampuan secara acak.
Kemampuan tersebut bisa Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, atau Divine.
Tidak ada pilihan untuk menentukan kekuatan awal. Sistem harus melakukan random generation.
2. GRAFIK DAN VISUAL
Gunakan:
2D Pixel Art berkualitas tinggi.
Resolusi pixel konsisten dan tajam.
Gaya pixel art seperti game RPG indie modern.
Animasi karakter yang halus.
Detail lingkungan sangat kaya.
Efek skill dengan partikel pixel.
Pencahayaan dinamis.
Bayangan monster dan karakter.
Efek hujan, kabut, malam, siang, dan perubahan cuaca.
Efek damage dan critical hit.
Visual harus terlihat seperti game pixel RPG premium, bukan pixel art sederhana atau kotak-kotak tanpa detail.
Kamera menggunakan top-down 2D atau 3/4 perspective.
Buat karakter, monster, NPC, dungeon, bangunan, pohon, senjata, dan lingkungan memiliki sprite masing-masing.
3. RANDOM AWAKENING SYSTEM
Ketika memulai permainan:
Pemain membuat nama karakter.
Pemain memilih penampilan dasar.
Pemain memasuki prolog cerita.
Sistem muncul untuk pertama kalinya.
Sistem melakukan Random Awakening.
Pemain mendapatkan satu kekuatan secara permanen.
Contoh kemampuan:
COMMON:
Enhanced Strength
Minor Regeneration
Night Vision
Wind Step
UNCOMMON:
Flame Manipulation
Ice Spear
Shadow Movement
Lightning Touch
RARE:
Blood Control
Spatial Slash
Phantom Clone
Soul Absorption
EPIC:
Gravity Manipulation
Necromancy
Time Perception
Dragon Transformation
LEGENDARY:
Void Manipulation
Monarch's Authority
Eternal Flame
Celestial Sword
MYTHIC:
Reality Distortion
World Devourer
Absolute Shadow
Divine Creation
DIVINE:
Origin Authority
Absolute System
Primordial Existence
Setiap kemampuan harus memiliki:
Nama.
Deskripsi.
Rarity.
Level kemampuan.
Damage.
Cooldown.
Mana cost.
Passive effect.
Active skill.
Evolution path.
Kekuatan tidak boleh hanya berbeda nama. Setiap kekuatan memiliki mekanisme gameplay berbeda.
4. STATUS CHARACTER
Buat panel status RPG:
Level
EXP
HP
MP
Strength
Agility
Vitality
Intelligence
Perception
Luck
Defense
Attack Power
Critical Chance
Critical Damage
Setiap naik level, pemain mendapatkan status points.
Pemain bisa mendistribusikan poin secara bebas.
Tambahkan sistem statistik tersembunyi seperti:
Potential
Soul Capacity
Adaptability
Resistance
5. SYSTEM INTERFACE
Sediakan UI sistem futuristik berwarna biru gelap dengan aksen ungu.
Menu utama:
[ STATUS ] [ SKILLS ] [ INVENTORY ] [ EQUIPMENT ] [ QUEST ] [ DUNGEON ] [ BESTIARY ] [ ACHIEVEMENTS ] [ MAP ] [ SETTINGS ]
Ketika sistem memberikan pesan, munculkan kotak notifikasi seperti:
[SYSTEM]
Congratulations, Player.
Your awakening has been completed.
Unique Ability Acquired: [ RANDOM ABILITY ]
Rarity: [RANDOM RARITY]
Your journey begins now.
6. COMBAT SYSTEM
Buat sistem pertarungan real-time.
Fitur:
Basic attack.
Heavy attack.
Dodge.
Dash.
Skill combination.
Critical attack.
Enemy targeting.
Boss mechanics.
Combo counter.
Stamina management.
Mana management.
Pemain bisa bertarung menggunakan:
Sword
Dual Sword
Dagger
Spear
Greatsword
Bow
Staff
Magic
Bare Hands
Setiap senjata memiliki animasi dan gaya bertarung berbeda.
7. DUNGEON SYSTEM
Dungeon muncul secara acak di berbagai wilayah.
Jenis dungeon:
Forest Dungeon
Ancient Ruins
Underground Cave
Forgotten Castle
Abyss Dungeon
Dragon Nest
Cursed Temple
Shadow Realm (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing game repository.

## Requirements
- Deliver a dark-fantasy, story-driven open-world RPG with exploration, dungeons, monster hunting, leveling, loot, equipment, bosses, and original world/story inspired by (but distinct from) Solo Leveling.
- First awakening must randomly and permanently grant one ability across Common through Divine rarity; abilities need distinct mechanics, stats, skills, passive effects, and evolution paths.
- Include character creation, RPG stats and hidden stats, futuristic system UI, real-time combat, multiple weapon styles, varied dungeons, and responsive phone/tablet support.
- Pixel-art visuals should be detailed, animated, and include lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Build now without clarification; note reasonable assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based game implementation.
- Use an original setting and ability system; starting ability is random.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a substantial HTML/CSS/JavaScript game foundation and procedural art modules.
- Added local font assets and data definitions for rarity tiers and Common–Epic abilities.

### Active
- Implementing game systems and integrating the already-created art, UI, and ability data.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing game repository.
- Deliver an original dark-fantasy story-driven game with exploration, combat, progression, random awakening, dungeons, bosses, loot, and responsive controls.

## Requirements
- Use original worldbuilding and systems inspired by, but distinct from, Solo Leveling.
- Start with character creation and a prologue; randomly and permanently grant one ability across Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, or Divine rarities.
- Give each ability distinct mechanics, stats, skills, passive effects, and an evolution path.
- Include RPG stats and hidden stats, a futuristic system UI, real-time combat, multiple weapon styles, varied dungeons, and phone/tablet support.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art visuals, animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Build now without clarification; note reasonable assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Starting ability is randomly generated; no player choice.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a substantial HTML/CSS/JavaScript game foundation and procedural art modules.
- Added local font assets and rarity definitions plus Common–Epic ability data.

### Active
- Integrating art, UI, ability data, and implementing the game systems.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect project files for incomplete modules and JavaScript syntax/runtime errors.
2. Finish and connect the title/prologue, random awakening, HUD/menus, combat, progression, dungeons, save, and input systems.
3. Run and verify the game in a browser; fix issues and capture a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and random rarity rolls.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `assets/fonts/`: Local font assets.

## Important Context
- The user requested a playable game, not just a design document.
- Work was written directly into the repository; no commit or verification was reported.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing game repository.
- Deliver an original dark-fantasy story-driven game with exploration, combat, progression, random awakening, dungeons, bosses, loot, and responsive controls.

## Requirements
- Use original worldbuilding and systems inspired by, but distinct from, Solo Leveling.
- Start with character creation and a prologue; randomly and permanently grant one ability across Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, or Divine rarities.
- Give each ability distinct mechanics, stats, skills, passive effects, and an evolution path.
- Include RPG stats and hidden stats, a futuristic system UI, real-time combat, multiple weapon styles, varied dungeons, and phone/tablet support.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art visuals, animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Build now without clarification; note reasonable assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Starting ability is randomly generated; no player choice.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML/CSS game shell and procedural pixel-art modules.
- Added local font assets, rarity definitions, and Common–Epic ability data.

### Active
- Integrating art, UI, ability data, and implementing the game systems.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect project files for incomplete modules and JavaScript syntax/runtime errors.
2. Finish and connect the title/prologue, random awakening, HUD/menus, combat, progression, dungeons, save, and input systems.
3. Run and verify the game in a browser; fix issues and capture a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and random rarity rolls.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `assets/fonts/`: Local font assets.

## Important Context
- The user requested a playable game, not just a design document.
- Work was written directly into the repository; no commit or verification was reported.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing game repository.
- Deliver an original dark-fantasy game with exploration, combat, progression, random awakening, dungeons, bosses, loot, and responsive controls.

## Requirements
- Use original worldbuilding and systems inspired by, but distinct from, Solo Leveling.
- Start with character creation and a prologue; randomly and permanently grant one ability across Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, or Divine rarities.
- Give each ability distinct mechanics, stats, skills, passive effects, and an evolution path.
- Include RPG stats and hidden stats, futuristic system UI, real-time combat, multiple weapon styles, varied dungeons, and phone/tablet support.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art visuals, animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Build now without clarification; note reasonable assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Starting ability is randomly generated; no player choice.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML/CSS game shell and procedural pixel-art modules.
- Added local font assets, rarity definitions, and Common–Epic ability data.
- Inspected existing source modules and UI structure.

### Active
- Integrating art, UI, and ability data; implementing and connecting game systems.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining files and identify incomplete modules and JavaScript syntax/runtime errors.
2. Finish and connect title/prologue, random awakening, HUD/menus, combat, progression, dungeons, saving, and input systems.
3. Run and verify the game in a browser; fix issues and capture a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and random rarity rolls.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `assets/fonts/`: Local font assets.

## Important Context
- The user requested a playable game, not just a design document.
- Work was written directly into the repository; no commit or verification was reported.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing game repository.
- Deliver original dark-fantasy worldbuilding and a browser-based game with exploration, combat, progression, dungeons, bosses, loot, and responsive controls.

## Requirements
- Include character creation and a prologue; randomly and permanently assign an ability from Common through Divine rarity.
- Give abilities distinct mechanics, stats, skills, passive effects, and evolution paths.
- Include RPG stats, futuristic system UI, real-time combat, multiple weapon styles, varied dungeons, and phone/tablet support.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art visuals, animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Build without clarification; note reasonable assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; the player does not choose the ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML/CSS game shell, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and Common–Epic ability data.
- Added `src/main.js` with imports, game state, character creation, weighted rarity and ability roll, awakening display, prologue dialogue, HUD updates, XP/level progression, and initial enemy spawning.
- Added original Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Finish the game loop, rendering, movement, combat, skills, enemy AI, interactions, and dungeon/boss encounters in `src/main.js`.
- Implement system overlay tabs, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, and mobile input.
- Verify syntax/runtime and playability in a browser; fix issues and capture a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with world rendering, game loop, inputs, combat, skill effects, enemy behavior, and interactions.
2. Connect system menus, progression/loot, dungeon and boss flow, and persistent save/continue behavior.
3. Run syntax checks and launch the game; test desktop and mobile controls, then capture and inspect a browser screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements, including title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Current game state and partial implementation; primary file to continue.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and awakening weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; repository files were added as untracked in the last observed `git status`.
- `index.html` already loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `src/main.js` currently ends after `gainXp`; rendering, event handlers, and the animation loop remain to be implemented.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Build distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML/CSS game shell, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and Common–Epic ability data.
- Added `src/main.js` imports, game state, character creation, weighted ability roll, awakening display, prologue dialogue, HUD updates, XP/level progression, and enemy spawning.
- Added Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js` with rendering, game loop, movement, combat, skills, enemy AI, and interactions.
- Implement system overlays, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, mobile controls, progression/loot, and dungeon/boss flow.
- Verify syntax and runtime, test desktop/mobile playability in a browser, and capture/inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` from its current endpoint after `gainXp`.
2. Connect rendering, inputs, combat, enemy behavior, menus, progression, dungeons/bosses, and persistence.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Current partial game state, abilities, UI, and progression implementation.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and awakening weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; the previously observed `git status` showed repository additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `src/main.js` currently ends after `gainXp`; rendering, event handlers, and the animation loop remain to be implemented.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Build distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML/CSS game shell, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and Common–Epic ability data.
- Added partial `src/main.js` for game state, character creation, weighted ability roll, awakening display, dialogue, HUD, XP/level progression, and enemy spawning.
- Added Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities.
- Added initial world rendering, map setup, pixel-art props/enemies/player, minimap, weather/night lighting, particles, basic attacks, ability casting, dodging, potions, and loot/boss defeat handling in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Finish the `src/main.js` game loop, movement/input handling, enemy AI, interactions, and state updates.
- Implement system overlay pages, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, touch controls, dungeon/boss flow, and progression/loot integration.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `dodge()`; implement input/event handlers and the update loop.
2. Connect prologue interactions, menus/system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, and dungeon progression.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently includes partial initialization, rendering, combat, and abilities, but lacks a complete loop and handlers.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and awakening weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `src/main.js` currently ends after `dodge()`; wiring and update/render loop remain incomplete.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG, **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Build distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML/CSS game shell, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and Common–Divine ability data.
- Added partial `src/main.js` for character creation, weighted ability roll, awakening display, dialogue, HUD, XP/level progression, and enemy spawning.
- Added initial rendering and combat code in `src/main.js`, including map and props, player/enemy sprites, minimap, lighting/weather, particles, attacks, ability casting, dodging, potions, loot, and boss-defeat handling.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: input/event handlers, update loop, movement, enemy AI, interactions, and state updates.
- Implement system overlay pages, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, touch controls, dungeon/boss flow, and progression/loot integration.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `dodge()` with input handlers, world updates, enemy AI, interactions, and the game loop.
2. Connect prologue interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, and dungeon progression.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends after `dodge()` and lacks completed wiring and loop.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and awakening weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- Recent implementation references `elapsed`, `heroSprites`, `state.equipment`, and `state.projectiles` and relies on wiring that is not yet present.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML/CSS game shell, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and Common–Divine ability data.
- Added partial `src/main.js` for character creation, weighted ability roll, awakening display, dialogue, HUD, XP/level progression, and enemy spawning.
- Added initial rendering and combat code: map and props, player/enemy sprites, minimap, lighting/weather, particles, attacks, ability casting, dodging, potions, loot, and boss-defeat handling.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` with input/event handlers, movement, enemy AI, interactions, and game loop.
- Implement system overlay pages, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, touch controls, dungeon/boss flow, and progression/loot integration.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `dodge()` with input handlers, world updates, enemy AI, interactions, and game loop.
2. Connect prologue interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, and dungeon progression.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends after `dodge()` and lacks completed wiring.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and awakening weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- Recent implementation references `elapsed`, `heroSprites`, `state.equipment`, and `state.projectiles`; required wiring remains incomplete.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the initial HTML/CSS game shell, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and Common–Divine ability data.
- Added partial `src/main.js` for character creation, weighted ability roll, awakening display, dialogue, HUD, XP/level progression, enemy spawning, rendering, and combat actions.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` with input/event handlers, movement, enemy AI, interactions, and game loop.
- Implement system overlay pages, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, touch controls, dungeon/boss flow, and progression/loot integration.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `dodge()` with input handlers, world updates, enemy AI, interactions, and game loop.
2. Connect prologue interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, and dungeon progression.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends after `dodge()` and lacks completed wiring.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and awakening weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- Recent implementation references `elapsed`, `heroSprites`, `state.equipment`, and `state.projectiles`; required wiring remains incomplete.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Rebuilt the beginning of `src/main.js` with game state, character creation, randomized awakening, prologue dialogue, HUD, enemy spawning, and ascendant ability definitions.

### Active
- Continue `src/main.js`: the latest version currently stops after `spawnEnemy()` and does not include the previously implemented world rendering and combat code.
- Implement world updates, enemy AI, input handlers, interactions, overlays/system tabs, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, touch controls, dungeon/boss flow, and progression/loot.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `src/main.js` and continue implementing from `spawnEnemy()`; account for the latest rewrite having removed the previous rendering/combat section.
2. Connect prologue interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, and dungeon progression.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Current partial game implementation; currently ends after `spawnEnemy()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Rarity definitions and awakening weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- The latest `src/main.js` rewrite truncated the earlier partial implementation: restore/reimplement rendering, combat, and all missing wiring.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Rebuilt the beginning of `src/main.js` with state, character creation, randomized awakening, prologue dialogue, HUD setup, enemy spawning, and ascendant ability definitions.

### Active
- Continue `src/main.js`, which currently ends after `spawnEnemy()`.
- Implement world rendering and updates, enemy AI, combat and skills, input/interactions, system tabs, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, touch controls, dungeon/boss flow, progression, and loot.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from `spawnEnemy()`, including world drawing, combat, and game loop.
2. Connect prologue and interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, dungeon progression, and loot.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Partial game implementation; currently ends after `spawnEnemy()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `src/main.js` imports `RARITIES`, `rarityOf`, `clamp`, `dist`, `weightedPick`, `rand`, `randInt`, and `pick`; `weightedPick` returns the selected value directly, so `rollAbility()` may need correction where it reads `.value`.
- `src/art/index.js` exports `weaponIcon`, `armorIcon`, and `consumableIcon`; `weaponIcon` and others are procedural asset helpers.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Built the beginning of `src/main.js` with game state, character creation, randomized awakening, prologue dialogue setup, HUD setup, enemy spawning, and ascendant ability definitions.
- Fixed `rollAbility()` to use `weightedPick()`’s returned rarity value directly rather than reading `.value`.

### Active
- Continue `src/main.js` from `spawnEnemy()`: implement rendering and updates, AI, combat and skills, controls/interactions, system tabs, inventory/equipment, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, progression, and loot.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from `spawnEnemy()`, including world rendering, combat, and game loop.
2. Connect prologue and interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, dungeon progression, and loot.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Partial game implementation; currently ends after `spawnEnemy()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` now accounts for this.
- `initArt()` initializes the procedural art registry; `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, and NPC sprites are available afterward.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Built the beginning of `src/main.js`: state, character creation, randomized awakening, prologue dialogue setup, HUD setup, enemy spawning, and ascendant ability definitions.
- Updated `rollAbility()` to use `weightedPick()`’s returned rarity value directly, with a fallback ability.

### Active
- Continue `src/main.js` from `spawnEnemy()`: implement rendering and updates, AI, combat and skills, controls/interactions, system tabs, inventory/equipment, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, progression, and loot.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from `spawnEnemy()`, including world rendering, combat, and the game loop.
2. Connect prologue and interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, dungeon progression, and loot.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Partial game implementation; currently ends after `spawnEnemy()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier repository status showed additions as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- `initArt()` initializes the procedural art registry; `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, and NPC sprites are available afterward.
- No syntax or browser testing has been performed yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Implemented the beginning of `src/main.js`: state, character creation, randomized awakening, dialogue, HUD setup, enemy spawning, ascendant abilities, and initial map generation.

### Active
- Continue `src/main.js`: rendering and updates, AI, combat and skills, controls/interactions, system tabs, inventory/equipment, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, progression, and loot.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing rendering, combat, and the game loop in `src/main.js`.
2. Connect prologue and interactions, system tabs, persistence, inventory/equipment, touch controls, dungeon progression, and loot.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Partial game implementation; currently ends after `spawnEnemy()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- `initArt()` initializes procedural art registries; `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, and NPC sprites are available afterward.
- No syntax or browser testing has been performed yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Implemented character-awakening setup, prologue dialogue, HUD initialization, enemy spawning, ascendant abilities, and initial map generation in `src/main.js`.
- Added foundational combat and progression systems: attacks, skills, enemy damage/loot, XP and leveling, item generation, healing/mana potions, and dodge.
- Added world/dungeon map setup, quest updates, and awakening display logic.

### Active
- Finish the `src/main.js` game: rendering and update loop, enemy AI, interactions, system tabs, inventory/equipment, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, and touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing rendering, updates, AI, controls, and interactions in `src/main.js`.
2. Connect system tabs, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, dungeon progression, and loot.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently includes creation/awakening, map setup, dialogue, foundational combat, skills, loot, and leveling, but no completed game loop.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no syntax or browser testing has been performed.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- `initArt()` initializes procedural art registries; `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, and NPC sprites are available afterward.
- The current `src/main.js` ends after `const camera={x:0,y:0};`; referenced functions such as `updateHud()` and `saveGame()` still need implementation.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement distinct abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Implemented character-awakening setup, prologue dialogue, HUD initialization, enemy spawning, ascendant abilities, and initial map generation in `src/main.js`.
- Added foundational combat and progression systems: attacks, skills, enemy damage/loot, XP and leveling, item generation, healing/mana potions, and dodge.
- Added world/dungeon map setup, quest updates, and awakening display logic.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and update loop, enemy AI, interactions, system tabs, inventory/equipment, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, and touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement rendering, updates, AI, controls, and interactions in `src/main.js`.
2. Connect system tabs, inventory/equipment, saving/loading, dungeon progression, and loot.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; creation, awakening, maps, dialogue, foundational combat/skills/loot/leveling are present; game loop and UI wiring remain incomplete.
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI elements for title, creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no syntax or browser testing has been performed.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- `initArt()` initializes procedural art registries; `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, and NPC sprites are available afterward.
- `src/main.js` currently ends after `const camera={x:0,y:0};`; referenced functions such as `updateHud()` and `saveGame()` still need implementation.
- Combat and ability handlers were recently added, including `getMods`, `playerDamage`, `attack`, `damageEnemy`, `killEnemy`, `checkXP`, `addParticle`, `makeItem`, `useSkill`, `usePotion`, and `startDodge`; several ability kinds and systems remain unhandled.
