## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game shell, styling, procedural pixel-art modules, local fonts, rarity data, and ability data.
- Implemented character setup, awakening reveal, dialogue, map generation, enemy spawning, combat, skills, loot, XP/leveling, potions, and dodge in `src/main.js`.
- Added HUD update logic and system overlay pages for status, skills, inventory, equipment, quest, dungeon, bestiary, achievements, map, and settings.
- Added item equip flow and basic dungeon entry flow in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js` with rendering, enemy AI, interactions, controls, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, and touch controls.
- Wire DOM event handlers and gameplay transitions, including save/load and system controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with rendering, update loop, enemy AI, map interactions, and controls.
2. Connect UI event handlers, persistence, dungeon progression, boss flow, loot pickups, and touch input.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; core game and UI functions exist, but game loop and event wiring remain incomplete.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/`: Procedural pixel-art tiles, props, heroes, monsters, bosses, item icons, and registry.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `start.sh`: Existing game startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- `initArt()` initializes registries; `art.tiles` maps tile IDs to arrays of canvases, `art.props` maps prop names to arrays of canvases, and `art.monsters` maps types to animation-frame arrays.
- `buildHeroSprites()` provides `down`, `up`, and `side` frame arrays.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement abilities and evolution paths, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Recreated the initial portion of `src/main.js`: imports, game state, hero preview helpers, ability data, map setup, character creation, awakening reveal, and ability rolling.
- Added extra ascendant abilities for Legendary, Mythic, and Divine; generic Rare/Epic entries were also added.

### Active
- Continue implementing `src/main.js` beyond `populateAwakening()`: dialogue, combat, progression, rendering, enemy AI, interactions, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, UI event handlers, and touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` from the end of `populateAwakening()`; most gameplay functions, UI wiring, and the game loop are currently absent.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Current partial implementation; currently ends after `populateAwakening()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, system overlay, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Initializes procedural art registries and exposes sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Tile IDs and procedural tile canvases used for map rendering.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery including chests, portals, rifts, houses, and other props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `src/main.js` was replaced during this work and currently contains only the initial implementation through awakening setup; earlier checkpoint gameplay functions are not present in the current file.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js` as an ES module.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries: `art.tiles` maps tile IDs to arrays of canvases (water/lava are nested animation-frame arrays); `art.props` maps prop names to arrays; `art.monsters` and `art.bosses` map types to animation-frame arrays; `buildHeroSprites()` provides `down`, `up`, and `side` frame arrays.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Rebuilt `src/main.js` with imports, game state, UI helpers, character preview, ability pools and awakening, map generation, character initialization, and awakening UI.
- Added generic Rare/Epic entries and custom Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities with passives, evolutions, and skills.
- Added starting town and dungeon map layouts with prop and NPC placement.

### Active
- Continue `src/main.js` beyond `populateAwakening()`: dialogue, combat, progression, rendering, enemy AI, interactions, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, UI event handlers, and touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from the end of `populateAwakening()`.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Current implementation; ends after `populateAwakening()`, so most gameplay and UI wiring remain absent.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Tile IDs and procedural tile canvases.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- The worktree contains untracked project files; `src/main.js` does not exist in `HEAD`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `src/main.js` contains imports, game state, UI helpers, character preview, ability pools and awakening, map generation, character initialization, and awakening UI.
- Added generic Rare/Epic entries and custom Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities with passives, evolutions, and skills.
- Added starting town and dungeon map layouts with prop and NPC placement.
- Inspected the game shell in `index.html` and procedural art registry/modules.

### Active
- Continue `src/main.js` after `populateAwakening()`: dialogue, combat, progression, rendering, enemy AI, interactions, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, UI event handlers, and touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from the end of `populateAwakening()`.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Current implementation; ends after `populateAwakening()`, so most gameplay and UI wiring remain absent.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Tile IDs and procedural tile canvases.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- The worktree contains untracked project files; `src/main.js` does not exist in `HEAD`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `src/main.js` has imports, game state, UI helpers, character preview, ability pools and awakening, map generation, character initialization, and awakening UI.
- Added generic Rare/Epic entries and custom Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities with passives, evolutions, and skills.
- Added starting town and dungeon map layouts with prop and NPC placement.
- Inspected `index.html`, styling, procedural art registry/modules, abilities, rarity data, and shared utilities.

### Active
- Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `populateAwakening()`: dialogue, combat, progression, rendering, enemy AI, interactions, persistence, dungeon/boss flow, UI event handlers, and touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` from the end of `populateAwakening()`.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Current implementation; ends after `populateAwakening()`, so most gameplay and UI wiring remain absent.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Tile IDs and procedural tile canvases.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `src/main.js` does not exist in `HEAD`; project files are untracked.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `src/main.js` has character setup, awakening presentation, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP and evolution, loot drops, basic/skill combat, and damage handling.
- Core game shell and HUD, character creation, awakening, dialogue, system overlay, and touch-control elements exist in `index.html`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after the combat and progression helpers; required functions such as `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; currently missing the game loop, rendering, UI wiring, persistence, and remaining systems.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `src/main.js` currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` still need implementation.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and HUD, character creation, awakening, dialogue, system overlay, and touch-control elements exist in `index.html`.
- `src/main.js` includes character setup, awakening presentation, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP and evolution, loot drops, basic/skill combat, and damage handling.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after the combat and progression helpers; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; remaining systems and game loop are unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `src/main.js` currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and HUD, character creation, awakening, dialogue, system overlay, and touch-control elements exist in `index.html`.
- `src/main.js` contains character setup, awakening presentation, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP and evolution, loot drops, basic/skill combat, and damage handling.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; systems and game loop remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `src/main.js` currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and HUD, character creation, awakening, dialogue, system overlay, and touch-control elements exist in `index.html`.
- `src/main.js` has character setup, awakening presentation, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP and evolution, loot drops, basic/skill combat, and damage handling through `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; systems and game loop remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `src/main.js` currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.

2:

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.

20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.

- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and HUD, character creation, awakening, dialogue, system overlay, and touch-control elements exist in `index.html`.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening presentation, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP and evolution, loot drops, basic/skill combat, and damage handling through `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `buildProps()` in `src/art/props.js` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- The HTML contains system tabs for status, skills, inventory, equipment, quest, dungeon, bestiary, achievements, map, and settings.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and HUD, character creation, awakening, dialogue, system overlay, and touch-control elements exist in `index.html`.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening presentation, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP and evolution, loot drops, basic/skill combat, and damage handling through `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for title, character creation, awakening, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `buildProps()` in `src/art/props.js` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- Recent inspection confirmed the HTML includes required HUD, dialogue, overlay, ending, and touch-control element IDs; `main.js` has no event listeners yet.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide the game shell, title and character-creation screens, awakening reveal, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening presentation, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP and evolution, loot drops, basic/skill combat, and damage handling through `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, dialogue, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `buildProps()` in `src/art/props.js` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- The HTML includes the referenced HUD, dialogue, ending, and touch-control element IDs; `main.js` has no event listeners yet.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` has partial implementations for character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, and combat through `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, dialogue, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and hero sprite arrays from `buildHeroSprites()`.
- `buildProps()` in `src/art/props.js` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` includes referenced HUD, dialogue, ending, and touch-control element IDs; `main.js` has no event listeners yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` partially implements character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, and combat through `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, dialogue, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `buildProps()` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` contains the HUD, dialogue, overlay, and touch-control IDs; no event listeners are present in the current `main.js`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` partially implements character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, and combat through `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, persistence/load flow, HUD and system overlay, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `castSkill()`; `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `updateHud()`, and `saveGame()` are referenced but missing.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main game implementation; currently ends at line 66 with `castSkill()`.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, dialogue, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `buildProps()` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- An attempted edit to append the missing game functions failed because its `oldString` did not match exactly; no code was changed by that attempt.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, and combat through `castSkill()`.
- Added `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, save/load, HUD updates, interactable lookup, and minimap rendering after `castSkill()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, HUD system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after the newly added helpers; the file still lacks the main render/update loop and event initialization.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently includes combat and newly appended helpers but still needs the main loop and input wiring.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `buildProps()` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `showEnding()`, `updateQuest()`, `saveGame()`, `loadGame()`, `updateHud()`, `nearbyInteractable()`, and `drawMinimap()` are now defined in `src/main.js`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, combat, and helper functions through `drawMinimap()`.

### Active
- Complete dialogue, rendering and game loop, enemy AI, interactions, HUD system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `drawMinimap()` with game rendering/update loop and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; still lacks the main render/update loop and input wiring.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `buildProps()` returns arrays keyed by prop type; `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

input.oldString: function drawMinimap(){const c=el('minimap');if(!c||!map.tiles.length)return;const g=c.getContext('2d');g.clearRect(0,0,c.width,c.height);const sx=c.width/map.width,sy=c.height/map.height;for(let y=0;y<map.height;y++)for(let x=0;x<map.width;x++){const t=map.tiles[y][x],col=state.dungeon?(t===9?'#171a27':t===13?'#47534d':'#3b4050'):(t===4?'#17415f':t===3?'#897251':t===2?'#203829':'#315d3a');g.fillStyle=col;g.fillRect(x*sx,y*sy,Math.ceil(sx),Math.ceil(sy));}for(const e of state.enemies){if(!e.dead){g.fillStyle=e.boss?'#ff637a':'#d78383';g.fillRect(e.x/map.worldW*c.width-1,e.y/map.worldH*c.height-1,3,3);}}g.fillStyle='#fff0a0';g.beginPath();g.arc(state.player.x/map.worldW*c.width,state.player.y/map.worldH*c.height,3,0,Math.PI*2);g.fill();}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, combat, persistence, and core simulation.

### Active
- Finish rendering and the game loop, dialogue/interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with world rendering, dialogue/interactions, system tabs, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; rendering, game loop, and remaining interactions/input are unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` has character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, combat, persistence, HUD/minimap, and portions of simulation implemented.

### Active
- Finish rendering and game loop, dialogue/interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after line 126 with world rendering, dialogue/interactions, system tabs, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; rendering, interactions, and input wiring remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` has partial implementations for character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, persistence, and HUD/minimap.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and game loop, dialogue/interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js`, beginning after the currently available code around line 126.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; rendering, interactions, and input wiring remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project context and usage information.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` has partial implementations for character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, persistence, and HUD/minimap.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and game loop, dialogue/interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js`, beginning after the currently available code around line 126.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; rendering, interactions, and input wiring remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project context and usage information.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` has partial implementations for character setup, awakening, map generation, enemy spawning, dungeon transitions, XP/evolution, loot, persistence, and HUD/minimap.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`, including rendering and game loop, dialogue/interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js`, beginning after the currently available code around line 126.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; rendering, interactions, and input wiring remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project context and usage information.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project context and usage information.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `src/main.js` already defines `update()`, `handleDeath()`, and `collectLoot()`; the implementation continues from the closing brace of `collectLoot()` at line 126.
