messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- The first 126 lines of `src/main.js` implement partial character setup, awakening, map and enemy creation, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and game loop, dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after line 126, completing rendering, interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at line 126, with rendering, interactions, and input wiring unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project context and usage information.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `src/main.js` already defines `update()`, `handleDeath()`, and `collectLoot()`; the implementation continues from the closing brace of `collectLoot()` at line 126.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- The first 126 lines of `src/main.js` implement partial character setup, awakening, map and enemy creation, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.
- Inspected art registries, tile definitions, utilities, HTML structure, and system-overlay styling.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and game loop, dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after the unfinished `collectLoot()` function, completing rendering, interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at line 126, with rendering, interactions, and input wiring unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- The first 126 lines of `src/main.js` implement partial character setup, awakening, map and enemy creation, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.
- Inspected relevant screen/control IDs, art registries, tile definitions, utility functions, and ability data.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and game loop, dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after the unfinished `collectLoot()` function, completing rendering, interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at line 126, with rendering, interactions, and input wiring unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- The first 126 lines of `src/main.js` implement partial character setup, awakening, map and enemy creation, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.
- Inspected UI IDs, art registries, tile definitions, utility functions, ability data, and relevant system-overlay styles.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and game loop, dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after the unfinished `collectLoot()` function, completing rendering, interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at line 126, with rendering, interactions, and input wiring unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- The dialogue, system overlay, tabs, and touch controls are already present in `index.html`; relevant visual styles are in `styles.css.
- Additional inspected UI styles include status, skills, inventory, equipment, quest, and dungeon layouts in `styles.css`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- The first 126 lines of `src/main.js` implement partial character setup, awakening, map and enemy creation, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.
- Inspected ability data, art registries, tile definitions, UI elements, and system-overlay styling.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: rendering and game loop, dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after the unfinished `collectLoot()` function, completing rendering, interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at line 126, with rendering, interactions, and input wiring unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` includes tabs for status, skills, inventory, equipment, quest, dungeon, bestiary, achievements, map, and settings; `styles.css` has corresponding layouts.
- `package.json` was not found at the repository root.

- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- The first 126 lines of `src/main.js` implement partial character setup, awakening, map and enemy creation, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.
- Inspected relevant ability data, art registries, tile/prop definitions, UI elements, and system-overlay styling.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` after the unfinished `collectLoot()` function: rendering and game loop, dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `collectLoot()`, completing rendering, interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and capture/inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at line 126, with rendering, interactions, and input wiring unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns tile arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` includes tabs for status, skills, inventory, equipment, quest, dungeon, bestiary, achievements, map, and settings; `styles.css` has corresponding layouts.
- `buildProps()` includes assets such as `tree`, `torch`, `pillar`, `chest`, `portal`, `rift`, `house`, and `smithy`.
- No `package.json` was found in the repository.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- The first 126 lines of `src/main.js` implement partial character setup, awakening, map and enemy creation, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` after the unfinished `collectLoot()` function: rendering and game loop, dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `collectLoot()`, implementing rendering, interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at line 126, with rendering, interactions, and input wiring unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` includes system tabs for status, skills, inventory, equipment, quest, dungeon, bestiary, achievements, map, and settings; styles are in `styles.css`.
- `buildProps()` includes assets such as `tree`, `torch`, `pillar`, `chest`, `portal`, `rift`, `house`, and `smithy`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, and simulation updates.
- Added pixel-world rendering and the animation loop to `src/main.js`, including tiles, props, enemies, hero, effects, lighting, and weather.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` with dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

- (none)

1. Continue `src/main.js` after the new `frame()` function; implement remaining interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, simulation updates, pixel-world rendering, and the animation loop.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` with dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `frame()`; implement remaining interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at the animation loop, with interactions and controls unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, simulation updates, pixel-world rendering, and animation loop.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` after `frame()` with dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` after `frame()`; implement remaining interactions, overlays, and input wiring.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at the animation loop, with interactions and controls unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` includes selectors for all system tabs, dialogue, character-creation controls, HUD actions, and mobile controls, but `src/main.js` still needs to wire them.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, simulation updates, pixel-world rendering, and animation loop.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` after the animation loop; wire existing screens, controls, dialogue, and system tabs.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at the animation loop, with interactions and controls unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` includes selectors for system tabs, dialogue, character creation, HUD actions, and mobile controls, but `src/main.js` still needs to wire them.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, simulation updates, pixel-world rendering, and animation loop.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` after the animation loop; wire existing screens, controls, dialogue, and system tabs.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at the animation loop, with interactions and controls unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, simulation updates, pixel-world rendering, and animation loop.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` after the animation loop; wire existing screens, controls, dialogue, and system tabs.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at the animation loop, with interactions and controls unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for screens, HUD, overlay, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and touch-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, simulation updates, pixel-world rendering, and animation loop.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` after the animation loop; wire existing screens, controls, dialogue, and system tabs.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` with dialogue and interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at the animation loop, with interactions and controls unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements for creation, HUD, dialogue, system tabs, ending, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- Recent inspection confirmed `index.html` includes creation, dialogue, awakening, system tabs, ending, and mobile controls; `src/main.js` currently has 150 lines and ends at `requestAnimationFrame(frame);`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` implements character setup, awakening, maps, enemies, combat, progression, loot, persistence, HUD/minimap, simulation updates, pixel-world rendering, and animation loop.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` by wiring existing screens, controls, dialogue, and system tabs; add remaining interactions and dungeon progression.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement dialogue/interactions, system tabs, dungeon progression, and keyboard/touch controls in `src/main.js`.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently ends at the animation loop, with interactions and controls unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM elements for creation, dialogue, awakening, system tabs, ending, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`. Syntax and browser testing have not been performed.
- `weightedPick()` returns the selected value directly; `rollAbility()` uses it directly.
- Art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `getMonsterFrame()` looks up monster and boss sprite frames.
- `index.html` includes creation, dialogue, awakening, system tabs, ending, and mobile controls. `src/main.js` currently has 150 lines and ends at `requestAnimationFrame(frame);`.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` currently contains recreated setup, ability data, map setup, basic enemy spawning, and dungeon entry/exit foundations.

### Active
- Rebuild/finish `src/main.js`: the previous implementation was overwritten during this session, and the current file stops at `leaveDungeon()`.
- Implement combat, progression, persistence, rendering, UI wiring, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `src/main.js` and supporting files; continue implementation from the current `leaveDungeon()` endpoint.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently incomplete and ends at `leaveDungeon()`.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM elements for creation, dialogue, awakening, system tabs, ending, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registries and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprite generation.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Existing art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Preserve and extend the current `src/main.js`; its earlier combat, simulation, and renderer code is no longer present.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` has a partial foundation: state and ability data, map setup, enemy spawning, dungeon entry/exit, character setup, and awakening UI.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`, which currently ends at `leaveDungeon()`: combat, progression, persistence, rendering, UI wiring, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from the current `leaveDungeon()` endpoint.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently incomplete.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI elements.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Existing art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` has a partial foundation for state, abilities, map setup, enemy spawning, dungeon entry/exit, character setup, and awakening UI.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js`, currently ending at `leaveDungeon()`: combat, progression, persistence, rendering, UI wiring, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from the current `leaveDungeon()` endpoint.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently incomplete.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project overview and usage context.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Existing art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `index.html` exposes the UI IDs for HUD, ten system tabs, dialogue, awakening, and touch controls; the main implementation must wire these existing elements.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` includes a partial foundation for state, abilities, map setup, enemy spawning, dungeon entry/exit, character setup, and awakening UI.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js`, currently ending at `leaveDungeon()`: combat, progression, persistence, rendering, UI wiring, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` from the current `leaveDungeon()` endpoint.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently incomplete.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project overview and usage context.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Existing art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `index.html` exposes the UI IDs for HUD, ten system tabs, dialogue, awakening, and touch controls; the main implementation must wire these existing elements.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- `src/main.js` has foundation logic for state, abilities, map setup, enemy spawning, dungeon entry/exit, character setup, and awakening UI.
- Added functions to `src/main.js` for save/load, XP and evolution, combat attacks, skill casting, potions, and dodging.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js`: the new combat functions are not yet wired to game updates/rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Verify syntax and runtime; test desktop/mobile playability in a browser and inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` after `dodge()`, including game loop, rendering, UI wiring, dialogue, system tabs, and controls.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop and mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently incomplete and recently extended with combat/progression helpers.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project overview and usage context.
- `start.sh`: Project startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `HEAD`.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Existing art registries include `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, and `art.bosses`; `buildHeroSprites()` provides hero frames.
- `buildTiles()` returns arrays keyed by tile ID; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- `index.html` exposes the UI IDs for HUD, ten system tabs, dialogue, awakening, and touch controls; the main implementation must wire these existing elements.
- `src/main.js` currently ends after the newly added `dodge()` function; functions already added include `saveGame()`, `loadGame()`, `xpGain()`, `damageEnemy()`, `attack()`, `castSkill()`, and `usePotion()`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- Repository includes art assets and RPG data modules.

### Active
- Recover and complete `src/main.js`. It was just overwritten with empty content, replacing its prior implementation.
- Wire gameplay updates/rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty after the latest tool action; its former implementation may need recovery from Git history or other repository state.

## Next Move
1. Inspect repository/Git state and recover `src/main.js` if possible; otherwise rebuild the game entry point using the existing HTML, styles, art, and data.
2. Implement and wire the game loop, rendering, UI, dialogue, system overlay, and controls.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop/mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main implementation; currently empty due to the latest write action.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.
- `README.md`: Project overview and usage context.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were noted as untracked in `HEAD`.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Before `src/main.js` was emptied, it contained state/map setup, ability awakening, persistence, XP/evolution, combat, skills, potions, and dodge helpers; the conversation record includes much of that source.
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, and `buildHeroSprites()`. `buildTiles()` values are arrays, with water/lava using nested frame arrays.
- `index.html` exposes IDs for HUD, ten system tabs, dialogue, awakening, and touch controls; these need wiring.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- Repository project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in Git.

### Active
- Rebuild `src/main.js`, which is currently empty, using the existing HTML, styles, art, and data.
- Wire gameplay updates/rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- The previous `src/main.js` implementation cannot be recovered from Git history: repository reports no commits for that file, and project files are untracked.

## Next Move
1. Implement the game entry point in `src/main.js`.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop/mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water/lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; implement sensible shared mechanics for them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Procedural art registries and supporting ability/rarity data are present.
- Inspected relevant HTML IDs, utility functions, art APIs, tile structures, and ability definitions.

### Active
- Rebuild `src/main.js`, currently empty, as the game entry point.
- Wire gameplay, rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.

## Next Move
1. Implement the game entry point in `src/main.js`.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop/mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water/lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; implement sensible shared mechanics for them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Repository project files are uncommitted and appear untracked.
