messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `styles.css` provide game screens, HUD, dialogue, system overlay, ending, and mobile-control elements.
- Inspected UI IDs, shared utilities, art registry APIs, tile structures, and ability/rarity data.

### Active
- Build `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is currently empty.
- Wire gameplay, rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.

## Next Move
1. Implement the game entry point in `src/main.js`.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop/mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water/lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; implement sensible shared mechanics for them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist; only `low.js` and `mid.js` were found.
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the main UI structure, ability and rarity data, art registry, hero sprites, and tile identifiers.
- Confirmed the ability data currently includes Common–Uncommon in `src/data/abilities/low.js` and Rare–Epic in `src/data/abilities/mid.js`.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is currently empty.
- Wire gameplay, rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.

## Next Move
1. Implement the game entry point in `src/main.js`, using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for desktop/mobile; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Procedural enemy sprites.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Procedural boss sprites.
- `src/art/props.js`: Procedural scenery and interactive props.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; use shared mechanics where appropriate.
- `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist; Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Starting weapon path remains selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the main UI structure, ability and rarity data, art registry, hero sprites, and tile identifiers.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is currently empty.
- Wire gameplay, rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

## Repository findings

- **Game UI and DOM hooks:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` contains the game’s UI markup and IDs. It includes the HUD, title and character-creation screens, dialogue, awakening reveal, system tabs, item modal, toast layer, mobile controls, loading screen, and ending screen. The system tabs use `data-tab`; touch actions use `data-action`; character options use attributes such as `data-hair`, `data-color`, and `data-path`. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css` styles the UI.

- **Implementation caveat:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` loads `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js` as a module, but `main.js` is empty (0 bytes). The entry point currently has no application initialization or game logic.

- **Art APIs:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/art/index.js` is the central art registry. It initializes tile, prop, monster, boss, and NPC art and exports helpers such as `getMonsterFrame` and `getMonsterIcon`, plus item-icon, hero, portrait, and preview functions. Art is procedurally generated on canvases; `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js` provides shared canvas and pixel-drawing helpers.
  - Related modules: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/art/items.js`, `heroes.js`, `tiles.js`, `monsters.js`, `bosses.js`, and `props.js`.

- **Ability data:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/abilities/low.js` and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/abilities/mid.js` contain ability records. Records include fields such as `id`, `name`, `rarity`, `color`, `sigil`, `tagline`, `desc`, `passive`, `evolution`, and `skills`. Skill records include gameplay values such as `kind`, `mana`, `cd`, damage, range, duration, and color.

- **Rarity data:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/rarity.js` defines rarity records, lookup maps, and `rollItemRarity`. Its rarities run from common through divine.

- **Runtime scripts:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh` are runtime wrappers. `startup.sh` only contains strict-shell setup. The README is project boilerplate.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and a selectable starting weapon.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Finish without clarification and note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Keep the starting weapon selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the main UI structure, ability and rarity data, art registry, hero sprites, and tile identifiers.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is currently empty.
- Wire gameplay, rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- User’s latest request: “play”.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Ability awakening is randomized; players do not choose their ability.
- Keep the starting weapon selectable during character creation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected UI structure, ability and rarity data, art registry, hero sprites, tile identifiers, monster/boss APIs, and shared utilities.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is currently empty.
- Wire gameplay, rendering, UI events, dialogue, system tabs, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Run syntax/runtime checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.
- The latest request is “play”; implement the game so it can be launched and played.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.
- Awakening ability and rarity are randomized; the player selects a starting path.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing HTML UI, procedural art APIs, utility functions, ability and rarity data, and monster/boss sprite definitions.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is currently empty.
- Connect the existing screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Test syntax and browser play on desktop and mobile; inspect a gameplay screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: Procedural art registry and sprite-frame lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Repository files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing HTML UI, procedural art APIs, utility functions, ability and rarity data, and monster/boss sprite definitions.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is empty.
- Connect the existing screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Test syntax and browser play on desktop and mobile; inspect a gameplay screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Repository files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing HTML UI, procedural art APIs, utility functions, ability and rarity data, and monster/boss sprite definitions.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point; it is currently empty.
- Connect the existing screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Test syntax and browser play on desktop and mobile; inspect a gameplay screenshot.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.
- Repository files are uncommitted and appear untracked.

## Findings

- **UI markup:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` contains the UI contract. Main interaction targets include:
  - **Game/HUD:** `game`, `hud`, `hud-portrait`, `hud-level`, `hud-name`, `hud-title`, `bar-hp/mp/sp/xp`, `txt-hp/mp/sp/xp`, `hud-time/day/weather/zone`, `minimap`, `mini-label`, `hud-quest`, `quest-collapse`, `quest-name`, `quest-objective`, `combo-meter/count`, `interact-prompt/text`, `ability-bar`, `slot-0/1/2`, `cd-0/1/2`, `icon-0/1/2`, `sname-0/1/2`, `slot-potion`, `slot-mana`, `potion-count`, `mana-count`, `hud-controls`, `system-btn`, `hud-gold`, `player-aura` (lines 16–82).
  - **Screens/creation:** `title-screen`, `btn-new`, `btn-continue`, `continue-label`, `btn-how`, `title-stats`; `creation-screen`, `creation-back`, `preview-canvas/name/path`, `char-name`, `btn-random-name`, `hair-options`, `hair-color-options`, `cloak-color-options`, `path-options`, `btn-begin` (lines 85–171).
  - **Dialogue/awakening/system:** `dialogue-layer`, `dialogue-portrait/speaker/text/choices/next`; `awakening-screen`, `awaken-name`, `ability-reveal`, `reveal-rarity/sigil/name/desc/stats/passive/skills`, `btn-accept-awakening`; `system-overlay`, `sys-portrait`, `sys-mini-name/level`, `sys-tabs`, `sys-clock`, `sys-kicker/title/gold/close/content` (lines 177–249).
  - **Shared UI/mobile:** `modal-layer`, `modal-card`, `toast-layer`, `touch-controls`, `joystick`, `stick`, `loading-screen`, `ending-screen`, `damage-vignette` (lines 255–283). Skill buttons use `data-skill="0|1|2"`; touch controls use `data-action`.

- **Utilities:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js` exports math/interpolation (`TAU`, `clamp`, `lerp`, `invLerp`, `dist`, `dist2`, `angleTo`, angle and easing helpers), random/noise (`mulberry32`, `seedRandom`, `randomSeed`, `rand`, `randInt`, `chance`, `pick`, `shuffle`, `weightedPick`, `hash2`, `valueNoise`, `fbm`), canvas/pixel/color helpers (`makeCanvas`, `px`, `pxl`, `shade`, `hexToRgba`, `roundRect`, `poly`), and formatting/game helpers (`fmt`, `roman`, `formatTime`, `timeLabel`, `dayCount`, `emitName`, `shortNum`, `clamp01`, `withinCone`). See lines 5–200.

- **Ability data format:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/abilities/low.js` and `mid.js` export `LOW_ABILITIES` and `MID_ABILITIES`, arrays of ability objects. Each has `id`, `name`, `rarity`, `color`, `sigil`, `tagline`, `desc`; a `passive: { text, mods }`; `evolution: [{ level, name, desc, mods }]`; and `skills: [...]`. Skill entries share `name`, `desc`, `kind`, `mana`, `cd`, `color`, with kind-specific fields such as `dmg`, `radius`, `duration`, `range`, `speed`, `mods`, or `summonType`. The rarity module `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/rarity.js` also exports `RARITIES`, `RARITY`, `RARITY_RANK`, `RARITY_COLOR`, `rarityOf`, `AWAKENING_WEIGHTS`, and `rollItemRarity`.

- **Art registry:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/art/index.js` exports the mutable `art` registry (`tiles`, `props`, `monsters`, `bosses`, `npcs`, `npcPortraits`, `ready`), `initArt()`, `getMonsterFrame(type, frame)`, and `getMonsterIcon(type, size = 50)`. Call `initArt()` before relying on populated registry fields. It also re-exports monster/boss/NPC metadata, hero/portrait helpers, item icon helpers, and tile constants.

- **Implementation caveat:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js` currently has no readable content, and no existing source code references the HTML IDs or imports the utilities/ability data. The markup and modules provide conventions, but no current integration behavior to mirror.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, ability and rarity data, art registry, and procedural hero, tile, monster, and boss APIs.
- Confirmed `src/main.js` is empty and no existing source code integrates the UI.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, ability and rarity data, art registry, and procedural hero, tile, monster, and boss APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No syntax or browser tests have been run.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, ability and rarity data, art registry, and procedural hero, tile, monster, and boss APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, ability and rarity data, art registry, and procedural hero, tile, monster, and boss APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No `package.json` was found in the repository root.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, a prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, ability and rarity data, art registry, and procedural hero, tile, monster, and boss APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- No prior `src/main.js` implementation can be recovered; Git history has no commits for it and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.

## Important Context

- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or browser tests have been performed yet; repository files are untracked.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or browser tests have been performed yet; repository files are untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or browser tests have been performed yet; repository files are untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or browser tests have been performed yet; repository files are untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or browser tests have been performed yet; repository files are untracked.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or browser tests have been performed yet.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or tests have been run yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
- No implementation or tests have been run yet.

## Objective
- Complete **ECLIPSE SYSTEM: THE LAST AWAKENED**, a playable browser-based 2D pixel-art action RPG in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Include character creation, prologue, randomized permanent ability awakening across Common–Divine rarity, and selectable starting weapon/path.
- Implement ability evolution, RPG progression, real-time combat, varied dungeons and bosses, loot, persistence, and responsive phone/tablet controls.
- Aim for detailed pixel-art presentation with animation, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, and environmental variety.

## Decisions
- Use procedural pixel-art assets and a browser-based implementation.
- Keep starting-path selection in character creation.
- Support Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities despite the lack of a dedicated data file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the HTML UI contract, utilities, rarity and ability data, and procedural art APIs.

### Active
- Implement `src/main.js` as the game entry point, connecting screens, dialogue, system tabs, gameplay loop, rendering, and desktop/mobile controls.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` is empty; Git history has no commits for it, and project files are untracked.
- Legendary, Mythic, and Divine abilities have no corresponding data file; `src/data/abilities/high.js` does not exist.

## Next Move
1. Implement `src/main.js` using the existing UI and procedural art APIs.
2. Run syntax checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; fix issues and inspect a screenshot.
3. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and UI element IDs; loads `src/main.js` as a module.
- `src/main.js`: Empty; needs the game entry point and primary implementation.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `src/utils.js`: Shared utilities, random selection, canvas helpers, and geometry.
- `src/art/index.js`: `initArt()`, art registry, and sprite lookup.
- `src/art/tiles.js`: Procedural tile canvases and tile IDs.
- `src/art/heroes.js`: Hero sprites, portraits, and preview rendering.
- `src/art/monsters.js`: Monster definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/art/bosses.js`: Boss definitions and sprite generation.
- `src/data/rarity.js`: Awakening rarity definitions and weights.
- `src/data/abilities/low.js`: Common and Uncommon abilities.
- `src/data/abilities/mid.js`: Rare and Epic abilities.

## Important Context
- Art APIs include `initArt()`, `art.tiles`, `art.props`, `art.monsters`, `art.bosses`, `buildHeroSprites()`, and `drawPreview()`.
- `buildTiles()` values are arrays; water and lava use nested frame arrays.
- Ability data defines multiple skill kinds and passive/evolution modifiers; shared mechanics can support them.
